why: Checks 1 and 2 test only behaviour the expect lines require: left-padding, the default space fill, and returning s unchanged when it is already long enough. Check 3 goes further than its words. "A section for every function" doesn't say what the heading must look like, but the regex only counts a heading at level ## or deeper that starts with the function name. A section titled "# padLeft" or "## Function: padLeft" would fail even though the line's words are met. Check 4 also goes further. "npm test passes" only needs exit code 0, but PASS also needs the summary to show the exact text '# fail 0'. That depends on which reporter is used: Node's default spec reporter prints "ℹ fail 0". These format and exact-wording rules sit inside PASS conditions rather than under Advisory.
